question: Can even immense material wealth justify giving the Kaula teaching to an unworthy person?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels represents immense wealth.
Someone may possess such an accumulation.
The verse raises this as a measure of value.
inference: Even wealth vast enough to fill the ocean with jewels is not a sufficient basis for transmission.
uncertainties: ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is a fused and irregular form; exact verbal analysis is uncertain
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to fill the ocean with jewels, it would not suffice.
